headline_insight_tags.When the agent goes quiet: clients/_smoketest/00_inputs/research/voc-reddit-dump-260611.md#L18 — same agent went quiet on the buy, q3

dcts.copy_1:
Your flat sold in three weeks. The same agent went quiet the moment you started buying.

You felt the reason before you could name it. On the sell side, a higher price pays them more. On the buy side, the better the deal they get you, the less they earn.

That is not a personality change. That is the structure.

The advice you most need — push for a lower price, flag the risky stack, tell you the unit is overpriced — is the advice they are paid not to give.

One structure cannot produce that conflict: a flat fee. S$4,500, the same whether you buy at S$900k or S$1.6m. Nobody earns more when you spend more.

You overpaid once. You said never again.

See the analysis on one shortlist unit for S$290, before you commit to anything.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.copy_2:
Your flat sold in three weeks. Then the same agent went quiet.

On the buy, the better your price, the less they earn. The incentive flipped.

A flat fee can't flip. See the maths on a real shortlist for S$290.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.cta: See the analysis on one shortlist unit for S$290, before you commit to anything.
dcts.angle_rationale: MP-01 already half-sees the wound. Their flat sold fast, then the same agent went quiet on the buy. Name the felt moment first, then hand them the mechanism: a flat fee is the one structure where the advisor cannot earn more when they spend more. Lead with the problem they live, introduce the flat fee as the named fix, prove it with checkable numbers. Contrast the fee structure, never the people. Buying emotion is relief, not opportunity.
dcts.why_am_i_testing_this: Tests whether naming the buy-side incentive flip plus a clean flat-fee mechanism beats commission-agent aspiration copy for a scarred L4 upgrader who has already overpaid once.

dcts.offer: T2 S$290 Shortlist Teardown -> T3 S$4,500 flat-fee advisory
dcts.diversity_map_entry: DM#4 (solution-aware; suspicion at hidden commission cost)
headline_drafts: The cost you never see itemised
dcts.copy_1:
S$4,500 for advice, when agents are free? That's the reflex. It's also the trap.

The free agent isn't free. The commission is baked into the price you pay. You just never see it itemised.

One flat fee, shown to you. See the method on your shortlist for S$290 first.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.copy_2:
The free agent isn't free. Their commission is built into the price you pay — you just never see it itemised. If a clear set of eyes stops you overpaying, the flat fee isn't the cost. It is the saving.

See the method on your shortlist for S$290.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.cta: See the method on your shortlist for S$290 first.
dcts.angle_rationale: MP-03 decides on logic. They are blocked by a pricing illusion: they think free is cheaper than S$4,500. Make the hidden commission visible and the math flips them fast. Lead with the reflex objection, expose the hidden cost, reframe the flat fee as the cheaper honest line item. Numbers they can re-run. Contrast the structure, never the people. Anti-hype tone because this buyer rejects outrage marketing.
